studies.title: Love And Compassion Placed Between
studies.meaning: Marriage appears here in a list of evidence, set beside the making of the heavens and the variety of human speech, which puts it in the category of signs rather than of arrangements. The purpose named is rest, and the verb behind it is the one used of settling into a dwelling. Two things are then said to be placed between the pair. The commentators generally distinguish them: one is the attraction that draws people together, the other the compassion that carries them once the first has quietened.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The surah opens with news of a Byzantine defeat and a prediction of recovery, then turns to a sequence of signs, of which this is one. Marriage in Arabia was a contract between families as much as between two people, negotiated with a payment and often intended to settle or prevent a dispute between clans. Listing it among the signs of God was not how that society usually spoke about it.

keyTerms.note: From the root that gives the words for dwelling and for stillness. What is described is not excitement but the ceasing of restlessness, the state of having somewhere to stop.

A warm liking that shows itself in wanting the other's company, distinct from desire and from duty. The word is used elsewhere of friendship, which keeps it from being read as a purely marital emotion.
The same word the Quran uses most often of God, and connected in Arabic to the womb. It carries protectiveness toward someone whose need you feel as your own.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: A household was often a single room or a tent, shared and unprivate. Men left for weeks with herds or with caravans, and a marriage was frequently arranged to bind two families rather than to satisfy two people. The word for settling would have carried the picture of a traveller setting down a load at the end of a stage, which is the ordinary sense the ayah is borrowing.
studies.didYouKnow: This ayah belongs to a run of four, each opening with the same phrase about God's signs and each closing with a different human faculty. The first ends with people who reflect, the next with those who know, the next with those who listen, and the last with those who use reason. The signs are the same for everyone; the closing clause changes what is being asked of the observer.
studies.theologicalSignificance: An ordinary human bond is treated as evidence for God, which means the evidence is not confined to the extraordinary. The affection is also located in a gift rather than in the couple's own achievement, and that changes what its absence means: something has not been received rather than someone having failed. The second of the two words placed between them is the word most often used of God Himself.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same verb of settling, tracing the pair back to a single origin before the resting is mentioned.
Gives the other image for the same closeness, each of the two described as clothing for the other.
Shows what this ayah describes turned into a request, joy in one's household asked for as a prayer.

studies.applyIt: This week do one thing for the person you live closest to that they will not find out about: a task removed before they reach it, a small expense absorbed, a complaint not made. The second word in this ayah describes care that does not require an audience, and the easiest way to test whether you have it is to remove the audience.

studies.title: Your Tongues And Your Colours
studies.meaning: Human difference is classed as evidence, not as a problem to be managed. The making of the heavens and the earth and the variation of human speech and complexion are set inside one sentence at the same level of proof, which is a considerable claim about the scale of the second item. The word for the differing carries succession as well as unlikeness, things following one another in turn. And the sign is assigned to those who know, so the reading of it is treated as a matter of knowledge.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The surah opens with news of a war between two distant empires and then turns to signs closer at hand. Mecca itself was a meeting point: the sanctuary and the trading season drew people speaking Aramaic, Persian, Greek and Abyssinian, and the early community included men and women who had come from Persia, Abyssinia and the Byzantine lands. Variation was not an abstraction to that audience.

keyTerms.note: From a root meaning to come after or take the place of another. The word covers both difference and succession, and the Quran uses it of night and day following one another as well as of unlikeness.
The plural of the physical tongue, used for language as English does. Keeping the bodily word means the sign is located in mouths and voices rather than in grammar or literature.
Those in possession of knowledge, as against the other closings in this passage, which name people who reflect, listen or reason. Here the sign is given to the ones who have learned something.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Mecca lived on arrivals. The pilgrimage and the fairs brought traders from Yemen, Syria, Abyssinia and the Persian Gulf, and interpreters made a living at the edges of the market. The early community reflected it: Bilal had come from Abyssinia, Salman from Persia, Suhayb from the Byzantine frontier. Those men prayed beside Meccans who had never left the valley.
studies.didYouKnow: The word translated as diversity here also means alternation, and the Quran uses it in exactly that sense elsewhere, for the alternation of night and day offered as a sign to people of understanding. The same noun therefore covers two kinds of variety: things unlike each other, and things taking turns.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Human variety is given a theological status rather than a merely social one. If difference is a sign, then flattening it or ranking it works against the evidence and not only against kindness. The pairing sets the scale, placing tongues and complexions beside the heavens and the earth. And the order within the ayah puts what people say ahead of how they look, which is the harder half to standardise.

crossReferences.why: States the purpose of the variety: peoples and tribes made so that they might come to know one another.
Says plainly that a single community was possible and was not what was intended, then sets a contest in doing good.
Repeats the point about one community, adding that people did not stop differing regardless.

studies.applyIt: Ask someone whose first language is not yours to teach you one greeting in it, said properly rather than approximately. Use it with them this week. The ayah names tongues before colours, and a language is the one difference a stranger can hand you a piece of in under a minute if you ask for it.

studies.title: The Pattern People Were Made On
studies.meaning: The instruction is to set the face toward the religion, an image of orientation rather than of an opinion adopted. What follows names it as the pattern on which human beings were originally made, so what is being asked for is described as a return to a default rather than the taking on of something new. Scholars differ over the clause about no altering of God's creation. Some read it as a statement that the original constitution cannot finally be replaced; others as a description of what should not be done to it.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The passage follows a comparison drawn from the listener's own life, about whether a man would make those who serve him equal partners in his property. The word used here for an upright inclination already had currency in Arabia before the message, attached to people remembered as having withdrawn from the idols without joining the Jewish or Christian communities around them.

keyTerms.note: From a root meaning to lean away from something toward something else. The word describes a turn already underway rather than a settled position, which is why it attaches to Abraham throughout the Quran.
From splitting open, used of a seed breaking soil and of dawn breaking. It names the state a thing is in when first brought out, before anything has been added to it.
From standing. Applied to a way of life it means both correct and self-supporting, the sense in which a wall is upright, so the claim is about structure rather than about correctness alone.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Orientation was a practical skill. A traveller set his face by a star or a known ridge and held it, and losing the line by a few degrees at the start meant missing the well by miles at the end. The image of setting the face toward something would have been heard as the beginning of a journey rather than as a posture, and a bearing was something you corrected repeatedly.
studies.didYouKnow: The word used here for the original human constitution comes from a root meaning to split or cleave open: it is used of a seed breaking through soil and of the dawn breaking the night. The same root gives the Arabic name for breaking a fast, which is why the festival at the end of the month of fasting carries it.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The claim being made is that belief in one God is not an addition to human beings but their starting condition, and that turning elsewhere is a departure from something already present. That changes what the invitation is: recovery rather than acquisition. It also explains the language just before it about following desire without knowledge, since a departure of that kind is described as drift rather than as a conclusion anyone reasoned their way to.

crossReferences.why: Describes the original acknowledgement being taken from human beings before any of this began.
Shows the same constitution surfacing under pressure, people calling on their Lord the moment harm touches them.
Attaches the same word for upright inclination to Abraham, before either of the later communities existed.

studies.applyIt: Watch for the next moment you turn to God without deciding to: a near miss in traffic, a phone call with bad news in it, a child slipping on stairs. Notice what came out of you before you had time to arrange it. This ayah is a claim about exactly that reflex, and you can only check the claim on your own evidence.

studies.title: Corruption On Land And Sea
studies.meaning: The opening verb means to come to the surface and become visible, so the damage is described as surfacing rather than starting. It is then attached to what human hands have earned, using the ordinary word for acquiring. What follows is a stated purpose, and it is not retribution: people are made to taste part of what they did so that they might come back. Commentators differ over the scope of the corruption, some reading it as moral disorder among people, others as visible ruin in the world, and many holding both.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The passage comes shortly after instructions on giving relatives, the destitute and the traveller their due, and after a contrast between wealth grown at other people's expense and wealth given away. The sequence connects what people do with money to what happens to the country around them. Mecca lived on routes across land that could not carry much pressure, and on shipping down the Red Sea coast.

keyTerms.note: From the back or the outer side of a thing. The verb means to become outwardly visible, which implies the condition existed before it could be seen and is only now showing.
The ordinary commercial word for gaining something by effort, used throughout the Quran of deeds. It treats actions as acquisitions a person accumulates rather than as events that merely happen.
A plain verb of physical return, the same word used of coming home. Naming it as the purpose puts the whole clause inside an invitation rather than inside a sentence of punishment.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Both arenas were economic facts. Pasture near a settlement could be grazed past recovery in a bad year, and clans quarrelled over wells and sometimes fouled them deliberately. Trees around Mecca were cut for fuel faster than the valley replaced them. On the water, the Red Sea route to Abyssinia carried grain and cloth, and a lost ship took a family's capital with it.
studies.didYouKnow: Land and sea are paired repeatedly in the Quran as a way of saying everywhere people can reach: God's knowledge is said to cover what is in both, guidance is given through the darkness of both, and human beings are described as carried on both. Here the same pairing is used to mark how far the damage extends.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Consequence is presented as instructive rather than as settlement. Only part of what was done is tasted, and the stated aim is return, which places even visible ruin inside an invitation rather than a verdict. Responsibility is assigned to human hands in the same sentence that keeps the outcome within God's arrangement, and the passage holds both without resolving the tension between them.

crossReferences.why: States the same connection between misfortune and what hands have earned, and adds that much is pardoned.
Gives the reverse case, blessings opened from sky and earth had the towns believed and been careful.
Describes the return this passage hopes for actually happening, and then not lasting past the relief.

studies.applyIt: Pick one ordinary habit of yours whose cost lands on someone you will never meet: what you throw away, what you buy without asking how it was made, water left running. Change it once this week, deliberately, and notice how small the change is. The ayah's word for return describes direction, and direction changes before distance does.

studies.title: The Traces Of His Mercy
studies.meaning: A mood is described before it is reversed. The word for the state people were in just before the rain covers the silence of someone who has run out of argument as well as out of hope. Then the instruction is not to watch the rain but to look at its traces, at what shows afterwards: the green that was not there a week ago. The argument for a resurrection is offered as something observed every year rather than as a doctrine to be accepted, and rain itself is named as mercy.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The lines sit in a run of signs in the surah's second half, following the description of winds gathering clouds and of people's visible relief when rain finally reaches them. In Mecca the raising of the dead was the point most often ridiculed by the objectors, and the surah answers it repeatedly from things they did not dispute rather than from claims they had already rejected.

keyTerms.note: From a root joining hopelessness to speechlessness. It describes someone whose expectation has collapsed and who has nothing left to say, which is more specific than sadness.
The word for footprints left in sand and for the remains of a camp. It points at evidence left behind by something that has passed, so the looking is directed after the event rather than at it.
The causative of living. The same verb governs both halves of the sentence, the ground and the dead, so the identical act is described twice rather than one being compared to the other.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Rain in that country arrived rarely and changed everything within days. A wadi that had been dry stone ran, grazing appeared where there had been gravel, and whole clans moved to follow it. When the rains failed, families sold animals and went to relatives. The despair named at the start of this passage was not a mood in general; it had a season attached and everyone had lived through one.
studies.didYouKnow: The clause about the earth being given life after its death occurs three separate times within this one surah, at ayat nineteen, twenty-four and here at fifty, in almost identical wording each time. The surah returns to the same sentence at intervals, attaching it first to resurrection, then to rain, then to both together.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The case for the raising of the dead is made from a repeated observation rather than from authority, which makes it checkable in the only way available to a listener. Naming rain as the traces of mercy has a further consequence: mercy is presented as something with visible effects in the world and not only as a disposition held toward people, and the invitation is to read the ground for them.

crossReferences.why: States the same movement earlier in the surah and draws the conclusion directly: thus will you be brought out.
Adds the detail of the ground stirring and swelling, then names the same power over the dead.
Runs the argument through a human life as well as through the reviving of dry ground.

studies.applyIt: After the next real rain where you live, wait two days and then go and look at one specific patch of ground you saw before it: a verge, a crack in a wall, a corner of a park. Look at what has changed rather than at the weather. The ayah asks for attention to the traces, which are always slower than the event.

studies.title: Do Not Let Them Unsettle You
studies.meaning: Two sentences close the surah, one about them and one to him. The first uses the word for a seal pressed into clay to close a letter, a metaphor of finality applied to hearts that will not know. The second names a subtler danger than persecution. The verb means to make someone light, to unsettle them into haste or into taking themselves less seriously than they should. What is being protected is steadiness rather than safety, and the anchor offered is that the promise is true.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, at the very end of the surah. The ayat just before it state that a miracle brought to the objectors would be dismissed as trickery, which describes a situation where argument has reached its limit. The instruction is addressed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and concerns the wearing effect of sustained ridicule rather than of physical danger. The commentators report no specific occasion for it.

keyTerms.note: The verb for pressing a signet into clay or wax to close something. It carries the sense of a document shut and marked, so that any later opening would be visible as tampering.
Built from lightness of weight. It covers being provoked into haste and being made to feel small at once, so what is warned against is losing gravity rather than losing courage.
From a root meaning settled knowledge that has stopped moving. Those described are not hostile so much as unanchored, which is what makes their company destabilising to someone who is anchored.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Seals were ordinary equipment. A merchant closed a sack or a letter with clay pressed by a signet ring, and the mark meant the contents were shut and any interference would show. Mockery was equally ordinary and far more dangerous socially: in a world where standing was held by reputation, poets were commissioned to make a man look light, and a successful verse could follow a family for a generation.
studies.didYouKnow: This surah opens with a statement about a specific near-term event, that the Byzantines, newly defeated, would be victorious again within a few years. It is one of very few places in the Quran where a political outcome is named in advance. The surah that begins with something to wait for ends with an instruction to wait steadily.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The closing instruction addresses morale rather than argument, which is itself worth noticing. The danger named is being destabilised by people who lack certainty, so confidence is treated as something that can be drained through company rather than only refuted. Patience here is not the endurance of pain. It is holding a position during a stretch when nothing in the visible situation confirms it.

crossReferences.why: Names the same pressure, a chest constricted by what they say, and gives a practice in response.
Addresses the same effect from the other side: let their speech not grieve you, since honour belongs to God.
Sets the measure for the patience being asked for, that of the messengers of firm resolve before him.

studies.applyIt: Notice the next remark that makes you want to move faster, post something, or explain yourself to someone who is not listening. Do none of those things for one hour. The word in this ayah describes being made light rather than being made afraid, and the test of weight is whether you can stay still while the remark is still fresh.
